findings.claim: Tree keyboard navigation moves selection but never moves DOM focus, so focus stays on the stale row and every subsequent Arrow key press re-computes from that old row's index — selection can never advance more than one step and the roving tab stop is broken.
findings.evidence: handleKey's ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End branches call only onSelectNode(target.id); TraceRow sets tabIndex={selected ? 0 : -1} but nothing focuses the newly selected row (the useEffect only calls scrollIntoView/virtualizer.scrollToIndex). Contrast run-trace-bar.tsx move() which explicitly calls items.current[next]?.focus(). This violates criterion 6.2 ('ARIA tree and roving tab stop, full tree keyboard handling').
findings.suggested_fix: After onSelectNode(target.id), focus the target row element (e.g. keep a rowElements map for all rows — not just the non-virtual path — and call rowElements.current.get(target.id)?.focus(), or focus in the scroll effect for the selected row).

findings.claim: The timeline scroll container's inline style={{ height: 256 }} overrides the flex-1 class, so the event tree is permanently pinned to 256px and can never grow within the min-h-[32rem] panel column.
findings.evidence: className="h-64 min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto ..." combined with style={{ height: 256, minHeight: 0 }} — inline style wins over the utility classes, defeating the flexible layout required by criterion 6.5.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the inline height and let flex-1/min-h-0 size the region, keeping only an explicit flex-basis or min-height if needed.

findings.claim: Checkpoint selection is a dead affordance: clicking a checkpoint only toggles aria-pressed; no checkpoint state/messages are rendered anywhere, and resumeLatestCheckpoint always resumes the latest checkpoint regardless of selectedCheckpointId.
findings.evidence: run-inspector.tsx checkpoint section renders only the list and a 'Resume latest checkpoint' button; run-trace-store.ts resumeLatestCheckpoint ignores state.selectedCheckpointId entirely and POSTs only artifact/input/session_id. Criterion 5.3 requires 'inert checkpoint inspection' — there is nothing to inspect.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the selected checkpoint's node_id/iteration/created_at (and optionally its state/messages as inert JSON) in the inspector, or remove the selectable buttons and show a static list.

findings.claim: The effect cleanup unconditionally disposes the module-singleton store's subscription, so any future second consumer of useRunTrace (or a remount ordering change) will tear down the live subscription out from under other mounted consumers.
findings.evidence: useRunTraceStore is created via zustand create() at module scope (run-trace-store.ts), while use-run-trace.ts runs `return () => { void useRunTraceStore.getState().dispose(); }` on every consumer unmount. The store API and generation guard suggest multi-context safety was intended, but unmount disposal is not reference-counted.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope disposal to context replacement (selectContext already unsubscribes the previous subscription), or track consumers and only dispose when the last one unmounts.

findings.claim: replayEnvelope only accepts three coarse path shapes (/a2ui/surfaces/{id}, .../components, .../dataModel) and throws on anything deeper, so any fine-grained JSON-patch path emitted by the backend (e.g. /a2ui/surfaces/main/components/root/children/0) makes the entire replay fail with 'Invalid A2UI replay path'.
findings.evidence: SURFACE_PATH = /^\/a2ui\/surfaces\/([^/]+)(?:\/(components|dataModel))?$/ and the final `throw new Error(\`Unsupported A2UI replay operation...\`)` in replayEnvelope; projectA2uiReplay propagates the throw, and refreshReplay surfaces it as a replay error state. The diff contains no evidence the backend restricts patches to these three shapes.
findings.suggested_fix: Support nested paths (apply value at the parsed sub-path) or document/verify the backend contract that replay patches are only whole-surface/whole-components/whole-dataModel replacements.

findings.claim: Response schemas use .strict(), so any additive backend field on checkpoints or the resume response (a backward-compatible wire change) fails validation and takes down the checkpoints/resume features entirely.
findings.evidence: checkpointSchema, checkpointListSchema, resumeResponseSchema and replayPatchSchema all end in .strict(); parseResponse throws 'returned an invalid response' on any unrecognized key. Criterion 3.2 requires typed validation but not strict-mode rejection of additive fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Use non-strict (strip) parsing for wire responses, or catch and log unknown keys without rejecting the payload.

findings.claim: useMessage is consumed in UserMessage and AssistantMessage but none of the shown import hunks add a useMessage import; if it was not already imported, the file fails typecheck.
findings.evidence: Hunks add `const messageId = useMessage((message) => message.id);` in two components, while the only import changes shown are MarkdownBubble, UarWordmark and chatMessageAnchorId — no addition to the @assistant-ui/react import is present in the diff.

findings.claim: The diff removes the only usages of RuntimeRunStepEntity, steps and TimelineRow but does not remove their import or the TimelineRow definition, leaving dead code that likely trips noUnusedLocals/lint gates.
findings.evidence: The hunk deletes `const steps = useEntities<RuntimeRunStepEntity>("RuntimeRunStep");` and the TimelineRow rendering, while the unchanged context still shows `} from "@/entities/types";` (the import of RuntimeRunStepEntity) and no hunk removes the TimelineRow function elsewhere in the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the RuntimeRunStepEntity import, the TimelineRow component and any now-unused helpers (statusTone/Badge if applicable).

findings.claim: Run handoff after resume updates only local state, not the ?run= query param, so refresh/back/share loses the resumed run selection — contrary to criterion 6.7's requirement to preserve route/query behavior.
findings.evidence: onRunHandoff={setSelectedRunId} is wired to RunTracePanel, but the only synchronization in the page is the one-way useEffect searchParams → setSelectedRunId; nothing calls setSearchParams when the selection changes.
findings.suggested_fix: In the handoff (and run selection generally), write the new run id into the search params (setSearchParams({ run: runId })).

findings.claim: selectPhase expands the phase node but not the root; if the user collapsed the root row, the phase stays invisible and projectRunTrace's visibility-based selection fallback silently replaces the requested selection with the first visible event.
findings.evidence: selectPhase does `new Set(current.expandedNodeIds).add(nodeId)` only for the phase id, and projectRunTrace computes selectedNodeId as `input.selectedNodeId && visibleRows.some(...) ? input.selectedNodeId : <fallback>`, so a collapsed root makes the phase selection vanish.
findings.suggested_fix: In selectPhase, also add the root id (projection.rootId) to expandedNodeIds before reprojecting.

findings.claim: The polite live region announces the identical string on every successful copy, so consecutive copies produce no DOM text change and screen readers will not re-announce.
findings.evidence:
setAnnouncement("Copied inspector JSON") sets the same literal each time into

{announcement}

.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear the announcement before setting it (e.g. setAnnouncement("") then set the message), or append a varying token.
